controls: Gate the RVV path on actual V availability consistent with the object's Tag_RISCV_arch v1p0/zve64d, with the scalar path as identical fallback.
Benchmark across the realized d distribution with the existing sq-encode benchmark (benchmark_QT_8bit_direct_*) and retain a scalar path/tail below the measured crossover.
Verify lane-exact byte output against the scalar reference before enabling the RVV path in production.
reasons: Special-value/out-of-range semantics: scalar fcvt.wu.s rtz saturates negative and >2^32-1 operands to 0 / 0xFFFFFFFF before byte truncation; a vector narrowing path (e.g. saturating vnclipu or unverified vnsrl) can change output bytes unless every lane matches the scalar byte output exactly.

Short-vector overhead: the 8bit_direct quantizer encode runs per vector with a known small dimension in the sq-encode bench; vsetvl/dispatch and tail costs can erase or invert the gain for small d, so an unconditional vector path may regress.

Store shape: the loop writes 1 byte per 4 bytes read, so after vectorization the residual bound may shift to L1 store/port throughput rather than ALU conversion; benefits must be verified on the target microarchitecture, not assumed from the lane count.

conditions.description: Hardware and the libfaiss.so build expose standard V (v1p0, zve64d, zvl128b, VLEN=128).
d is large enough for vectorization to clear vsetvl/dispatch and tail costs (crossover measured on target).
(uint8_t)x[i] conversion semantics (fcvt.wu.s rtz then byte truncation) are preserved for every call input.

actions.proposal: Add an RVV precision-conversion fast path to Quantizer8bitDirect::encode_vector (or make the existing V-capable build actually emit vector code for this template): a dynamic-vsetvl strip-mined loop that unit-stride loads x with vle32, converts f32->u32 with vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v (same round-toward-zero semantics as the current scalar fcvt.wu.s rtz), truncates to 8-bit via a narrowing shift vnsrl.wi shift 0 so the stored byte equals the (uint8_t)x[i] truncation of the conversion result, and stores with vse8; keep the scalar loop as the fallback and unchanged codec contract, with scalar tail handling for partial vl.

correctness_checks: Lane-exact byte output comparison vs scalar reference over 0, 255, negative, >255 (where defined), NaN, ±0.0, subnormals, and tail lengths (0, 1, VLMAX-1, VLMAX, VLMAX+1).
Zero-length and one-element vectors write the same bytes with no out-of-bounds access at the last partial vl.
With V disabled or unsupported, the binary still runs the scalar path and produces identical output.

expected_signals.signal: the scalar flw/fcvt.wu.s/sb sequence and the 100% hotspot at the scalar byte store 0x389728 disappear from the encode_vector hot interval
vsetvli, vle32, vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v, and vse8 instructions appear in the encode_vector disassembly and dominate the loop
benchmark_QT_8bit_direct_cpu_time_ns and encode_vector instructions-per-element decrease for mid/large d
sq-encode scalar-reference bytes and encode/decode round-trip outputs remain bit-identical

success_criteria: benchmark_QT_8bit_direct_real_time_ns and cpu_time_ns decrease on the target for the realized d distribution.
Encode_vector hot interval now contains vsetvli, vle32, vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v, and vse8 and instructions-per-element falls.

controls: Prefer the pointer form as preparation for or alongside the RVV precision-conversion fix, verified independently with instruction counts.
Confirm this->d is loop-invariant (const size_t, no concurrent mutation) before hoisting the limit.
Leave the semantic boundaries (zero-length early exit, per-byte store) untouched.
reasons: The gain is bounded to ~2-3 of 8 instructions per element (loop control), so a standalone source rewrite must not be treated as the primary fix while the scalar conversion stays dominant.

A source-level loop rewrite can perturb compiler scheduling or vectorization decisions and silently change codegen in the other direction; the correct contract for d as a const member (no mutation) must hold for the precomputed-exit rewrite to be legal.
Zero-length behavior and the early-exit branch must be preserved exactly, or the d=0 fast path changes.

conditions.description: A scalar path is retained (non-V builds or small d).
this->d is loop-invariant (const member) so the limit can be hoisted and end precomputed.
x and code are non-overlapping or aliasing is benign for pointer-increment traversal.

actions.proposal: Apply loop induction-variable strength reduction to the scalar encode loop: restructure the index-based loop so both x and code advance by pointer increment and the loop limit is fixed by a precomputed exit (end = code + d computed once from this->d, which is a loop-invariant const member) instead of recomputing add a4,a2,a5 and reloading ld a4,8(a0) every iteration; the same restructuring is subsumed by the RVV strip-mined fix if that path is adopted.

correctness_checks: d=0 executes zero loop iterations via the preserved early-exit path.
The last element writes code[d-1] exactly once and no iteration writes beyond code[d-1].
Element-by-element output matches the original index-based loop over small, large, and VLMAX-boundary lengths.

expected_signals.signal: the per-iteration ld a4,8(a0) limit reload and add a4,a2,a5 index-based address recompute disappear from the loop body
a precomputed end-pointer or hoisted single limit comparison appears as the loop exit condition
instructions-per-element in the scalar encode loop falls by roughly the loop-control share (2-3 of 8 instructions)
output bytes and branch-miss pattern remain unchanged

success_criteria: encode_vector disassembly no longer contains the per-iteration ld a4,8(a0) limit reload or the add a4,a2,a5 address recompute inside the loop.
Instructions per element in the scalar loop fall by the expected loop-control amount while output bytes stay identical.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Memory-bound hypothesis is refuted: L1 dcache load miss rate is 0.357% and LLC load miss rate is 2.356%, and cache_references (~19.38M) nearly equals cache_misses, so the working set is effectively cached; the conversion loop is dominated by instruction-stream work, not memory latency.

The conversion itself (fcvt.wu.s rtz) being per-lane is not the whole story only insofar as the value semantics are a single lane-independent instruction that maps exactly onto vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v; out-of-range/NaN value semantics are a correctness constraint on the fix, not an alternative root cause.

Sampling places all samples on the byte store, which could partially reflect store-queue/retire effects; however even allowing attribution skew, the 8-instruction scalar loop body (flw/add/addi/fcvt/addi/sb/ld/bltu) is the entire function and remains the sole hotspot.

findings.conclusion: The hot loop of Quantizer8bitDirect<SIMDLevel 0>::encode_vector is a fully scalar, per-element float->uint8 precision conversion (code[i]=(uint8_t)x[i]) — flw, fcvt.wu.s rtz, sb per lane with 100% of samples at the scalar byte store — containing zero v* instructions even though libfaiss.so is built with V (v1p0, zve64d, zvl128b); because the operation is lane-independent and cache-friendly, the workload cost is the scalar loop body and loop control, not memory, and the leverage point is an RVV precision-conversion formulation (vle32 + vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v + truncating narrowing + vse8).

neighbor_exclusions.reason: no_vectorization claims only a generic scalar main loop not explained by a more specific semantic row; this loop's dominant work is a required float-to-integer rounding/conversion and narrowing, which routes to the more specific precision-conversion row.

the elementwise-arithmetic row covers generic contiguous add/sub/mul/min/max and would under-specify the conversion; precision-conversion semantics (float-to-integer rounding + narrowing) dominate and are the routing source of truth.
the float32->uint8 conversion is necessary under the SQuantizer codec contract (input is float, code is packed uint8), not an unnecessary float64 round trip, so deletion does not apply.

findings.reasoning: Annotate (311c...) shows the whole function is a scalar loop at 0x389718-0x38972e: flw x[i], fcvt.wu.s rtz (float->u32 truncate), sb one byte, with 100% of samples at the store 0x389728, and zero v* instructions. Source (4507.../01b8...) shows the loop is code[i]=(uint8_t)x[i] (quantizers.h:318-320). Metadata (ed0...) proves libfaiss.so itself is built with Tag_RISCV_arch rv64i2p1_..._v1p0_..._zve64d1p0_..._zvl128b1p0, i.e. the object-level build ISA exposes standard V with 128-bit VLEN, so the hardware/build admission gate passes. Perf stat (b982...) rules out a memory bound (L1 miss 0.357%), so the lane-independent float->uint8 precision conversion loop is unvectorized scalar work on a V-capable build. This matches the precision-conversion signal: 'the main work in a scalar hot path is required float-to-integer rounding/conversion' executed per element with scalar conversion and narrow stores instead of RVV vfcvt/vnarrow/vse8.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The index-based codegen is a plausible compiler choice because the source loop is a plain for(i=0;i<d;i++) index loop and strength reduction is a codegen tuning detail rather than a semantic defect.

The impact is bounded to roughly 2-3 of the 8 instructions per element (address recompute add a4,a2,a5 and limit reload ld a4,8(a0)); the dominant cost is the scalar 32->8-bit conversion per element, so this is a contributing factor, not the root cause.

findings.conclusion: The compiler-generated encode loop also reconstructs the destination address each iteration (add a4,a2,a5) and reloads the loop bound d from 8(a0) in every pass (ld a4,8(a0) at 0x38972c) despite purely contiguous fixed-stride traversal, adding index/limit loop-control overhead per element that induction-variable strength reduction (pointer increments plus precomputed exit) would remove; this is a secondary contributing factor below the scalar-conversion root cause.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: the observed limit reload and per-iteration address recompute are loop-level induction-variable issues over a contiguous fixed-stride traversal, not peephole algebraic identities in a single basic block.

strong reduction only trims loop control; the primary cost is the scalar conversion which the RVV precision-conversion row owns; this codegen row is supporting for the contributing-factor conclusion only.

findings.reasoning: Annotate (311c...) traverses contiguous fixed-stride memory but recomputes the destination address every iteration (add a4,a2,a5 at 0x38971c, addi a5,a5,1 at 0x389720) and reloads the loop bound d from memory each pass (ld a4,8(a0) at 0x38972c) instead of pointer increments plus a single precomputed limit; this matches the loop_induction_variable_strength_reduction signal of per-iteration index scaling and limit reload in a contiguous loop. Perf stat (b982...) shows a small hot body where loop control is a large fraction of per-element cost. Because full vectorization (root cause conclusion) also removes these instructions, this is classified as contributing_factor with medium confidence.
